links.targetTitle: Satisfying every published Delegate requirement creates no e

title: Grove pays Delegates a flat monthly fee in arrears with clawback and an explicit denial that payment softens oversight
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.6 sets out five terms: Active Delegates receive a fixed USD amount per calendar month; the Grove Foundation administers payment from its approved operating budget; payment is "monthly **in arrears** and prorated for partial months"; eligibility requires the Delegate "to be in good standing and to have met responsibilities" during the covered period, with the Foundation able to "withhold or claw back amounts for non-performance or breach"; and — clause 5 — "**Compensation does not limit or waive any onboarding, renewal, or offboarding requirements**."

The structure is more informative than the amount. Pay is **flat**: it does not scale with delegated stake or with vote outcomes. That deliberately breaks two incentives a variable scheme would create — competing for delegations to raise income, and voting to please whoever supplies the stake. A delegate with a large following earns exactly what a small one earns, so the compensation channel carries no pressure at all.

Paying **in arrears** against met responsibilities converts the fee into settlement for work verified after the fact rather than a retainer, which is what makes withholding a live instrument rather than a threat requiring recovery.

Clause 5 is the defensive one, and it is aimed at an argument rather than a behaviour. A paid, ongoing, obligation-bearing relationship starts to resemble employment, and with that resemblance come expectations of notice, cause, and process before termination. Stating that compensation waives nothing pre-empts a delegate contesting an automatic offboarding on the grounds that they were being paid.

The combined design is a paid role with none of a job's protections, which is coherent given that removal is meant to be mechanical (three missed votes) or immediate (emergency grounds). Flat pay also sets the ceiling on what the scheme can buy: it secures **attendance**, which is what the offboarding rules measure, and nothing in the compensation structure rewards the quality of a vote.
description: Compensation is fixed rather than stake- or performance-weighted, conditioned on good standing and met responsibilities, and stated not to limit any onboarding, renewal or offboarding requirement.
